description: The long or effectful Execution operations a Node caller above the Execution tier reaches through src/native/execution-door.mjs (executionOp, runUnitInHost, launchSessionInHost): one host process per call, `fgos internal execution <op> --protocol 1`. Implemented by apps/fgos/src/wiring/execution_routes.rs.

invocation.request: The first line of stdin: one JSON object, the op's payload.
invocation.answer: One framed line on stdout: prefix, one JSON object, newline. Every other stdout line is an admission peer frame (contracts/admission-peer) or stray output and is never read as the answer.

exit.0: answered (a run-unit error result is an answer)
exit.3: host-version-mismatch: --protocol is not 1, checked before the op
exit.65: invalid-request: the payload is not a JSON object or misses a field

invocation.peer: run-unit and custody (with admit) ask the caller's case admission port over this process's stdout (requests) and stdin (answers), after the request line. The caller serves it with serveAdmissionPeer; pipes only. End of stdin: the caller keeps stdin open until it read the answer, so a run-unit process whose stdin ends after the request line treats the caller as gone and settles nothing for it. On unix it exits at once (status 1, no answer, no exit handlers; the supervisor holds the lent attempt lock and cwd lease). On Windows the controller holds a writing attempt's cwd lease, so it does not exit: the unit run goes on to its end, its peer calls failing closed (peer-closed), and the process then ends normally.

payload.request: the run-unit-request document (contracts/unit-run/run-unit.v1.json); an option outside its list is refused by name
payload.admission: boolean: the caller serves a case admission port; without it the run has none. The two events (unitRunCreated, caseAdmitted) always reach the caller.

run-unit.result: the run-unit-result document: { ok: true, result } or { ok: false, error } (the door rethrows the error's class)

payload.binding: object: bind()'s answer for the head seat (executor, invocation?, model, tier, reasoningEffort?, leaseAccount?, pool?)
payload.runnerConfig: object: the project's runner config (the default executor is applied by the host)
payload.key: string: the head key; .fgos/assignments/<key>/runs/01 is the attempt directory, used once
payload.opening: string: typed verbatim into the pane
payload.ceilingMs: number: the session's hard ceiling, positive
payload.env: object<string,string>?: added to the agent's launch environment
payload.workdir: string?: absolute path of a registered linked worktree of the project the attempt runs in; projectRoot when absent
payload.beside: string|null: the live key of the session whose tab the new one opens next to

result.placement: { host: 'terminal', key }: key is the attempt id
result.refused: { code, message, ...extra }: instead of the three fields above when the launch was refused (head-key-used, lease-refused with refusal, launch-unknown with launchState, or the code of the step that refused); the door rethrows it as an error carrying those fields

launch-session.implementation: launchSessionAttempt (src/runner/dispatch/session-attempt.mjs): engine transport_round::session_attempt over the host's AttemptDriver (apps/fgos/src/wiring/unit_run_host/session_attempt.rs); returns once the supervisor bound the attempt, never waits for the session to end (last at `85760c6f2`)

payload.admit: object?, the proposal asked of the peer's admit before the command runs

verify.subject: string?, what ran as the answer text names it (default Gate command)

result.admission: the peer's admit answer, when admit was given; a refused one runs nothing
result.admissionError: { code, message }? the peer could not answer
result.verified: the verify answer, when the command ran
result.answer: what a loop's verify hook is told, with verified
result.custodyError: { code, message }? custody could not be taken

result.verified: { verdict: pass|findings } or { infrastructure: timeout|not-run }, with status, how, tail, durationMs, outputDigest (runVerify)

result.adopt: the adopt verdict lines ({ v, protocol, attemptDir, state, outcome?, pendingStep?, reason? }) or null

result.requested: boolean: a cancel request is on disk for the attempt afterwards

result.ended: boolean: true once the gate is judged dead and adopt ran
result.adopt: the adopt verdict line ({ v, protocol, attemptDir, state, outcome?, pendingStep?, reason? })
result.refused: { code: no-binding|supervisor-alive|domain-not-scope|scope-mismatch|domain-not-ended, message }: instead of ended; the only processes ever signalled are the attempt's own scope unit and the binding's own gate record (by pid and start identity)

end-dead-attempt.implementation: end_dead_attempt in packages/run-supervisor/rust/src/controller/scope.rs; meant only for an explicit `fgos session stop` (src/session-host/head-stop.mjs is its one caller)

result.orphans: [{ runId, runDir, startedAt, wouldBecome, hasWorkerResult, reconciled? }]: the runs still marked running whose dispatch process is gone, each with the verdict a reader that cannot probe liveness gives it; written into run.json when reconcile is true

payload.purpose: string, optional: a capability row name or an executor id
payload.repoRoot: string, optional: resolves a tool's scanTarget and HEAD; the process cwd when absent

result.seat: { configured, executorId, executor?, bindingSource, tool?, invocationId?, binding?, refused? }: a registered executor of that name, else the tools serving it by live presence, else the seat Seat Binding binds for a row with a prefer pool of its own, else nothing configured
result.error: { name, code?, message }: a failure of the model other than a coded bind refusal; the door rethrows it

result.unserved: { <capability>: <registered name> }: each capability a tool executor declares whose every tool is missing or cannot be probed; labels and served tool abilities are left out
